text:
Maria Gomez: Heads up — noticed a p95 uptick on /chat for gold routes after yesterday's kernel selector change. started ~2109876400, steady since then :thinking:
Kevin Li: ack, what's the magnitude?
Maria Gomez: ~120ms -> ~240ms at p95 on long-seq (seq_len>1024) workloads, only gold tier. tail looks fine.
Arjun Patel: interesting. did the rollout include the new prefetch path for KV cache?
Maria Gomez: yes, kernel switch + enabling KV prefetch for routes we thought would benefit.
Sasha Ivanov: any profiling traces? can you paste perf counters or flamegraph snippet?
Maria Gomez: pasted below — lightweight perf sample after warmup:
```
# perf_summary
route: /chat (gold)
model: llama-2-13b
seq: 1400
p50: 50ms
p95: 240ms
kernel: fast-attn-v2
kv_prefetch: enabled
batch_mean: 4.1
queue_wait_mean: 18ms
kernel_switch_overhead: 35ms
prefetch_wait: 22ms
```
Maria Gomez: looks like kernel_switch_overhead + prefetch_wait are additive for these long sequences.
Priya Rao: could be microbatch composition: gold routes tend to be single-request bursts, batching heuristics may be waiting to reach batch token budget and prefetch blocks.
Kevin Li: what is the dynamic token budget config for gold right now?
Maria Gomez: current canary config on dedicated: `{ "route": "/chat", "tier": "gold", "token_budget_per_batch": 16000, "max_batch_size": 8, "queue_policy": "latency-first" }`
Arjun Patel: latency-first will try to close batches quickly, but token_budget high + KV prefetch means we prefetch heavy KVs per request, raising overhead. maybe lower token_budget for long-seq routes.
Sasha Ivanov: agree. suggestion: slice token_budget by median seq for route. e.g., token_budget = median_seq * 3 instead of absolute. For /chat median_seq ~600 so 1800 tokens budget instead of 16000.
Priya Rao: also consider turning prefetch to async fire-and-forget when kernel switch takes >20ms — don't block batch formation.
Kevin Li: can we A/B a two-variant canary? variant A: token_budget_per_batch=3000 + prefetcht_async=false; variant B: token_budget_per_batch=3000 + prefetch_async=true. Keep kernel selector change but toggle prefetch mode.
Maria Gomez: ok launching both in canary on 2 nodes each. will tag traffic by route-tier weight 5% gold.
perf-bot: Deploy event: canary variants created by @Maria Gomez at 2109876508 — IDs canary-A, canary-B.
Arjun Patel: quick note: add microtrace sampling for first 100 requests so we can attribute overhead to queue vs kernel swap vs prefetch.
Maria Gomez: good call — added microtrace hook. sample payload:
```
{"trace_id":"${RND}","route":"/chat","tier":"gold","queue_wait_ms":xx,"kernel_swap_ms":xx,"kv_prefetch_ms":xx,"model_infer_ms":xx}
```
Sasha Ivanov: after 10k requests in canary: preliminary numbers:
- baseline p95: 240ms
- canary-A p95: 160ms
- canary-B p95: 95ms
Maria Gomez: wow canary-B (async prefetch) looks much better. interestingly p50 unchanged.
Kevin Li: that suggests prefetch blocking was the culprit for tail. nice. Any regressions on silver routes?
Maria Gomez: negligible. silver kept same budget and prefetch disabled.
Priya Rao: we should also update batcher to prefer earlier dispatch if kernel_swap predicted to be heavy. make kernel_swap estimator part of queue policy.
Arjun Patel: agree — lightweight predictor based on (seq_len, model_variant, last_kernel). can return estimated_swap_ms and queue policy can subtract that from allowed wait.
Sasha Ivanov: I'll sketch a change: in QueuePolicy.evaluate(requests): compute budget_target = min(global_budget, sum(predicted_tokens) * factor) and candidate_dispatch_time = now + max_latency - max(predicted_swap_ms). If candidate_dispatch_time <= now then dispatch early.
Maria Gomez: sounds good. can we roll async prefetch + token_budget trim to prod for gold once canary hits 1% improvement on cost normal?
Kevin Li: set gate: p95 improvement >=10% and error rate unchanged for 24h. Also add gradual step from 5% -> 100% over 3 hours.
perf-bot: Canary metrics: canary-B p95 -61% vs baseline, errors +0.02% (within threshold).
Maria Gomez: starting prod rollout for gold with async prefetch + token_budget_per_batch=3000 + hysteresis 3-hour ramp at 2110000000.
Priya Rao: follow-up: schedule a perf-regression test that simulates long-seq bursts against canary config to ensure no cluster-level saturation.
Arjun Patel: also add a post-rollout job to log kernel switch counts per minute; if switch rate spikes we may need to pin kernel per pod for stable perf.
Sasha Ivanov: noted. I'll open a small PR with queue_policy changes and a unit test for predicted_swap_ms integration.
Maria Gomez: thanks all — will monitor post-rollout and capture full traces for the next retro. :thumbsup:
